name: François Hollande
summary: François Hollande, a Socialist, was President of France from 2012 to 2017: his government legalised same-sex marriage, he kept France's independent nuclear deterrent, declared the 2015 state of emergency, backed a financial transactions tax and the abolition of the death penalty worldwide, and framed his economic policy as deficit reduction with growth rather than austerity.

sources.title: EUSpeech: speeches by François Hollande as President of the French Republic, 2012-2015 (Schumacher et al., Harvard Dataverse XPCVEI; English machine translation of the French originals)
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: His public statements: UN General Assembly (25 Sept 2012), Kinshasa Francophonie summit (13 Oct 2012), nuclear deterrence at sea (4 July 2012), the Ferry tribute (15 May 2012), the energy transition and Fessenheim, tax havens and financial transactions tax, the responsibility to protect.

sources.title: EUSpeech: François Hollande's statements of 24 April 2013 (passage of the marriage law) and 14 November 2015 (state of emergency), reporting his own acts
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: His announcement that Parliament passed the law opening marriage to same-sex couples, which he had made his reform, and his declaration of a state of emergency after the Paris attacks.

sources.title: Loi n° 2013-404 du 17 mai 2013 ouvrant le mariage aux couples de personnes de même sexe, Légifrance (via the local LEGI corpus)
sources.author: French Parliament; promulgated by François Hollande
sources.usedFor: The marriage law of his presidency.

sources.title: UN General Assembly general-debate speeches of François Hollande, 2012-2016, UN General Debate Corpus
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: Renouncing the veto in mass atrocity, the UN's duty to act in Syria, two states for Israel and Palestine, the 2015 climate conference, ten percent of the financial transactions tax for development.

sources.title: Journal officiel, Congrès du Parlement, compte rendu intégral de la séance du 16 novembre 2015 (Versailles), declaration of the President of the Republic
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: His account of his own acts after the 13 November attacks: border controls restored, state of emergency proclaimed, extension of house arrest and administrative searches, a bill to extend and adapt the state of emergency, a constitutional revision.

sources.title: Loi n° 2013-504 du 14 juin 2013 relative à la sécurisation de l'emploi, art. 9 (employee representatives on boards), Légifrance (via the local LEGI corpus)
sources.author: French Parliament; promulgated by François Hollande
sources.usedFor: The job-security law that followed the January 2013 national agreement.

sources.title: EUSpeech: François Hollande's statement of 11 January 2013 on the job-security agreement
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: He hailed the agreement reached by employers and unions on his Social Conference method and listed what it would do: a personal training account, rechargeable unemployment rights, dearer short contracts, employee representatives with a vote on boards.

sources.title: Loi n° 2015-1501 du 20 novembre 2015 prorogeant l'application de la loi n° 55-385 du 3 avril 1955 relative à l'état d'urgence et renforçant l'efficacité de ses dispositions, Légifrance (via the local LEGI corpus)
sources.author: French Parliament; promulgated by François Hollande
sources.usedFor: The three-month extension of the state of emergency he asked for at Versailles.

sources.title: Loi n° 2015-912 du 24 juillet 2015 relative au renseignement, Légifrance (via the local LEGI corpus)
sources.author: French Parliament; promulgated by François Hollande
sources.usedFor: The intelligence law of his presidency.

sources.title: Loi n° 2016-1088 du 8 août 2016 relative au travail, à la modernisation du dialogue social et à la sécurisation des parcours professionnels, Légifrance (via the local LEGI corpus)
sources.author: French Parliament; promulgated by François Hollande
sources.usedFor: The labour law (loi El Khomri) of his presidency.

sources.title: Déclaration de M. François Hollande sur le projet de loi 'visant à instituer de nouvelles libertés et de nouvelles protections pour les entreprises et les actifs', La Plaine Saint-Denis, 1 March 2016, Élysée
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: His defence of the labour bill: giving firms the means to negotiate with staff representatives, more permanent contracts, the personal activity account.

sources.title: Déclaration de M. François Hollande sur l'abandon de la révision constitutionnelle relative à l'état d'urgence et à la déchéance de la nationalité, 30 March 2016, Élysée
sources.author: François Hollande
sources.usedFor: His account of the state of emergency (declared, extended twice), the anti-terror bill, intelligence coordination, more police, and dropping the constitutional revision.

sources.title: François Hollande, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of his career and presidency; no answer rests on it.

notes: First audit, in progress. EUSpeech (766 of his speeches, 2012-2015, English machine translation, so medium confidence at most) was searched by theme: marriage, secularism, death penalty, deterrence, nuclear energy, tax havens, financial transactions tax, the responsibility to protect, immigration, austerity and the deficit, trade unions, the minimum wage, retirement. The marriage law is cited as an action with his own statement of 24 April 2013. Searched without a settled answer: immigration, austerity, deficit and stimulus, unions and collective bargaining, the minimum wage, pensions, and the euro (his words describe aims without a position on the statements). His five UN General Assembly speeches 2012-2016 (UNGDC) and the Versailles Congress declaration of 16 November 2015 (Journal officiel, read by theme: state of emergency, borders, Syria, the constitutional revision) were read. Laws of his presidency are cited with his own announcing or defending statement: marriage 2013, job security 2013, state of emergency extension 2015, intelligence 2015, labour 2016. The 75% top tax (finance law 2013), the Responsibility Pact and CICE, the Macron law (2015) and the regional reform (2015) are not used: no statement of his own defending them was found open (vie-publique and elysee.fr were reached only for the three 2016 declarations above). The Mali intervention (counter-terrorism at Mali's request) and his 2013 Syria stance do not settle humanitarian-intervention, which stays on his UN words at low confidence.
